newsitem.title: USA: Travelers reports strong rise in profits.
newsitem.headline: Travelers reports strong rise in profits.

text.p: Travelers Group on Monday reported a strong rise in first-quarter profits, helped by cost savings and gains in its property-casualty and life insurance operations.
New York-based Travelers also was helped by record earnings at its Smith Barney brokerage unit.
Travelers Group reported first-quarter earnings of $642.1 million, up from $520.2 million a year ago. Earnings per share were a record 96 cents vs. 77 cents in the same period last year.
The earnings reflected two stock splits last year and the company's repurchase of 4.6 million shares in this quarter for employee benefit plans, Travelers Group said.
Revenues rose 31 percent to $5.93 billion from $4.51 billion.

"Life Insurance operations demonstrated strong earnings growth, both at Travelers Life & Annuity and Primerica Financial Services. At our 82 percent-owned Travelers Property Casualty Corp., .... we remain well ahead of our announced plan to achieve $300 million in annual cost savings by the end of 1997," Travelers Chairman Sanford Weill said in a statement.
The earnings beat Wall Street expectations, and Travelers Group stock rose $2 to $48.375 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Travelers Property Casualty Corp. earnings soared 132 percent to $267.9 million from $94.8 million in the same period last year. That figure excludes charges relating to the $4 billion aquisition of Aetna's property-casualty business in April 1996.

Travelers Property should continue to see impressive earnings growth for the next few quarters as it benefits from investment income growth and solid performance in its personal insurance lines, analysts said.
Weston Hicks, senior research analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein & Co., said his firm was recommending Travelers Property as an investment.
"The reason is that they are moving to a low-cost position in a consolidating industry, which could have a very significant payoff if they can make some additional acquisitions," Hicks said.
Weill has said Travelers is on the lookout for further property-casualty acquisitions.
Travelers has a reputation for growing by acquiring other companies and it likes companies where it can cut expenses and boost profitability almost immediately, analysts said.

Travelers' life and annuity business reported operating earnings of $101.1 million, up 22 percent from $82.6 million. The Primerica financial services unit had operating earnings of $78.1 million vs. $65.3 million.
The company's Smith Barney brokerage unit had record earnings of $238.9 million, up 7 percent from $223.9 million a year ago. Smith Barney's revenues rose 3 percent, to $1.66 billion.
Travelers's consumer finance unit had first-quarter operating earnings of $47.3 million, down 15 percent from $55.9 million a year earlier.
